title: Restore the pinned MIT YEIS Search/Places navigation semantics inside the current React shell and add Personal Signals as destinations

scope.subject: Universe search, curated places, personal-signal discovery, and direct system navigation

research_summary: The pinned MIT YEIS commit already contains a complete search UI and a curated Places model. More importantly, the vendored core already retains StarCatalog.search(), Universe.searchForeignBodies(), searchBlackHoles(), searchLandmarks(), galaxy search, and CameraController autopilot primitives. Rebuilding a separate site-search/index stack would duplicate these domain APIs. The selected approach reuses the MIT navigation semantics and existing search methods, adds only a thin React command-style shell, and treats Personal Signals as another destination class. cmdk/Fuse/Pagefind remain optional supplements if scale later exceeds the built-in search behavior.

sources.finding: Pinned MIT UI implements keyboard search across current/foreign bodies, catalogue stars, black holes, landmarks and galaxies, then navigates directly to the resolved astronomical target.
Pinned MIT UI provides grouped curated Places with typed destination kinds and stable refs instead of inventing a separate navigation database.
Vendored StarCatalog.search() already handles name/HIP/Gliese lookup and ranking.
Vendored Universe retains domain search helpers for foreign bodies, black holes and landmarks.

cmdk is a polished command-menu UI option, but adopting it now would add a UI dependency while YEIS already supplies the domain search semantics and the current shell needs only a small result surface.
Pagefind is optimized for generated document/site full-text search, not direct astronomical destination navigation.

search_ladder.conclusion: The selected mother engine already had Search and Places in its MIT UI. Restore those semantics instead of building an unrelated index product.
The current React/R3F shell can host the search surface while leaving search/routing semantics in the YEIS adapter.
StarCatalog and Universe already expose the actual search indexes needed by the navigator; reuse them directly.
cmdk/Pagefind can provide generic UI/indexing, but neither improves the current domain search enough to justify replacing the built-in YEIS behavior.

coverage_matrix.decision: Personal signals are injected as a destination class above the same result model.

coverage_matrix.capability: search astronomical stars using existing universe data
coverage_matrix.decision: Use StarCatalog.search() directly; do not build another star index.

coverage_matrix.capability: curated browseable places when query is empty
coverage_matrix.decision: Reuse the Places pattern and stable astronomical refs from the MIT UI.
Implement the small React interaction shell around reused YEIS results; no dependency is needed for the current scale.
Keep destination IDs compatible with CameraController centerOnDirection/goToPoint so spatial flight can be layered on without changing the navigator model.

candidates.name: Pinned MIT YEIS Search/Places semantics + thin React navigation shell
candidates.source: pinned MIT UI.ts/places.ts plus already-vendored StarCatalog/Universe APIs
candidates.license: MIT at e520568; existing upstream attribution retained
candidates.reason: Highest global reuse: keeps one astronomical index and one destination model, adds Personal Signals cleanly, and remains compatible with native YEIS camera autopilot later.

candidates.name: cmdk UI plus Fuse.js independent search index
candidates.reason: Strong generic UI/fuzzy search, but duplicates the astronomical search indexes already supplied by YEIS and adds dependencies without solving spatial destination semantics.

candidates.name: Pagefind-generated site index as primary navigator
candidates.reason: Excellent for static document search but mismatched to direct star/system destinations and would require a second mapping layer back into YEIS IDs.

decision.rationale: Restore the navigation semantics that already exist in the pinned MIT mother engine. Reuse StarCatalog/Universe search directly, expose curated Places and Personal Signals through one destination model, and keep the React layer limited to presentation and keyboard interaction.
decision.fallback: If result scale or fuzzy matching later becomes insufficient, layer Fuse.js or cmdk over the same destination API. If document/article search becomes a separate need, add Pagefind for documents without replacing universe navigation.
